indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER] presenting with jaundice and biological cholestasis. Evaluate for biliary obstruction, pancreatic malignancy, or choledocholithiasis.
technique: ** Helical CT imaging was performed from the diaphragm to the pubic symphysis following the administration of intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The liver demonstrates normal size and contour with homogeneous parenchymal enhancement. There is isolated dilatation of the right hepatic posterior sector bile ducts. Associated wall thickening is noted involving the right posterior duct, which is suspicious for an intrinsic lesion. The remaining intrahepatic biliary tree, including the left lobe and right anterior sector, appears non-dilated. The common hepatic duct and common bile duct are within normal limits for caliber, measuring 5 mm at the porta hepatis. No choledocholithiasis is identified. The gallbladder is present without wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid; no radiopaque stones are seen.
The pancreas is normal in morphology and attenuation. There is no focal mass, no evidence of pancreatic ductal dilatation, and no peripancreatic inflammatory changes. The spleen and adrenal glands are unremarkable in appearance.
Within the abdomen, there are a few small, simple hepatic cysts, the largest measuring 8 mm in segment IV, which are benign in appearance. There is mild atherosclerotic calcification noted along the abdominal aorta. No lymphadenopathy is identified in the retroperitoneum or mesenteric root.
The kidneys show symmetric excretion of contrast without hydronephrosis. The urinary bladder is well-distended with smooth walls. The bowel loops are non-dilated and demonstrate normal wall thickness throughout. No free intraperitoneal air or pleural effusions are visualized. The visualized lung bases are clear.
conclusion:
**
Isolated dilatation of the right hepatic posterior sector bile ducts with suspected thickening of the right posterior duct. No evidence of distal biliary obstruction or associated complications.
